title: Seasonal SOI cut next-quarter Nino 3.4 forecast error by 11% in 1981-2024, with uncertain gain
abstract: We tested whether mean seasonal air pressure improves next-quarter Nino 3.4 temperature forecasts beyond recent temperature history. Separate linear quarter fits used earlier years only. In 176 forecasts at 1981-2024 origins, adding SOI cut mean squared error by 11.45%. Root MSE fell from 0.4120 to 0.3877 C. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -0.24% to 20.60%. All four quarter-specific intervals included zero. A ten-year block interval and a common-trend check gave positive limits. The uncertainty conclusion thus depends on assumptions. Recent-period gain was 6.04%, with limits that included zero. These revised-data tests do not establish a stable forecast gain, physical cause or water supply benefit. Small samples, source revisions and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate errors, scores, a figure and numerical audits.

display.caption: Added SOI error reduction for 176 next-quarter forecasts at 1981-2024 origins. Blue bars give conditional 95% five-year block limits; gray bars give 98.75% limits. Q1 to Q4 are origin calendar quarters. The main pooled interval and all quarter intervals include zero.
